title: Revision and catch-up

stations.name: Lesson 1: Types of network
facts: LAN = local area network: one site, and the organisation owns the hardware.
The internet is the biggest WAN, joining networks all over the world.
The other three are all advantages of networks.

questions.a: A network covering a small area, such as one site, where the organisation owns the hardware

questions.q: Which is the best example of a WAN?
Which of these is a disadvantage of networking?
questions.a: Viruses can spread from one computer to others

stations.name: Lesson 2: Network performance
facts: Bandwidth is measured in bits per second. More bandwidth means more data can be sent at once.
Each user gets a smaller share of the available bandwidth, so everything slows down.
Video creates a lot of traffic. Extra cameras could use up bandwidth and slow the network for everyone, and the server needs enough storage too.

questions.a: The amount of data that can be sent in a given time, such as per second

questions.q: Thirty students start streaming video at the same time. Why does the network slow down?
questions.a: More users are sharing the same bandwidth

questions.q: The school wants more CCTV cameras recording video to the file server. What should the network manager check first?
questions.a: Whether the network has enough bandwidth for the extra video traffic

stations.name: Lesson 3: Client-server and P2P
facts: Clients request services and the server provides them. Connecting to the internet is the router's job.
The other three are advantages of client-server networks.
Every user's computer shares pieces of the file directly with the others, so they act as peers.

questions.q: In a client-server network, what does the server do?
questions.a: Provides services such as file storage, logins and backups to the clients

questions.q: Which of these is an advantage of a peer-to-peer network?
questions.a: It is cheaper to set up, because no expensive server is needed

questions.q: Torrenting downloads parts of a file from many other users' computers at once. Which model is this?

stations.name: Lesson 4: LAN hardware
facts: Switches work inside a LAN using MAC addresses. Routers join networks together using IP addresses.
A WAP sends and receives radio waves and is connected to the wired network by cable.
UTP is limited to about 100 m per run. Fibre works over kilometres, although it costs more.

questions.q: What is the difference between a switch and a router?
questions.a: A switch connects devices within a LAN; a router connects different networks, such as a LAN and the internet

questions.q: Which device lets wireless devices connect to a wired network?
Why is fibre optic used instead of UTP to link buildings that are far apart?
questions.a: It carries data much further with high bandwidth, and isn't affected by electrical interference

stations.name: Lesson 5: The internet
facts: The internet is the network of networks. The websites on it are the World Wide Web, which is a service that uses the internet.
DNS is made up of many domain name servers that look up the IP address for a domain name.
The other three are advantages of the cloud. Other disadvantages include ongoing costs and less control over your data.

questions.a: A worldwide collection of connected computer networks
Turns a domain name, such as www.google.com, into an IP address

questions.q: Which of these is a disadvantage of using the cloud?
questions.a: It relies on a stable internet connection

stations.name: Lesson 6: Star and mesh
facts: The switch is a single point of failure.
Mesh networks have many routes between devices, so there is no single point of failure.
Routers connect to several other routers, but not to every one of them.

questions.q: In a star network, what happens if the central switch fails?
Why is a mesh network more reliable than a star network?
questions.a: Data can be rerouted along another path if a link fails

questions.q: The internet is an example of which topology?

final.name: Final challenge: DNS

questions.q: Put the steps in order, from typing the address to seeing the page.
questions.a: You type www.google.com into the browser → The browser asks a DNS server for the IP address of www.google.com → DNS servers look up the domain name, asking other DNS servers if they need to → The IP address is sent back to the browser → The browser uses the IP address to request the page from the web server, which sends it back

final.note: Students should have predicted this on the worksheet before tapping the star.

common: Naming a term without saying what it does.
Giving an advantage with no reason attached.
Repeating the question in the answer.
